Overview

Engineer intelligent systems — from first principles to production.

An engineering-grade, 120-session program: production Python, statistics and classical ML, deep learning and computer vision with TensorFlow, Transformers built from scratch, advanced RAG and agentic systems, fine-tuning and alignment — then DSA, SQL and MLOps with FastAPI and Docker.

Starts from Python foundations, then moves fast into engineering depth.

Built for

  • Developers and engineers moving into AI engineering
  • Data scientists going deeper into deep learning and LLMs
  • Computer-science students and graduates
  • Technical professionals building AI products

Outcomes

What you’ll be able to do.

  1. Write production-grade Python — OOP, decorators, generators, concurrency, type hints, Pydantic and pytest
  2. Master statistics, feature engineering and every major classical ML family, with SHAP and LIME interpretability
  3. Build deep networks in TensorFlow: CNNs, ResNets, YOLO detection, segmentation and Vision Transformers
  4. Implement attention and a complete Transformer from scratch, and understand GPT-style decoding
  5. Architect advanced RAG — hybrid search, reranking, GraphRAG, CRAG — and multi-agent systems with LangGraph and MCP
  6. Fine-tune LLMs with LoRA and QLoRA and align them with RLHF and DPO
  7. Ship models with MLflow, FastAPI and Docker, and prepare for DSA and SQL interviews

Projects & capstones

7 things you’ll build.

  1. 01 Day 15

    End-to-End Extraction Pipeline

    A multi-page scraper built with OOP, type hints and decorators, cleaned with Pandas and exported to SQLite or Parquet.

  2. 02 Day 45

    End-to-End ML Pipeline

    Target encoding, SMOTE and XGBoost in an sklearn pipeline, validated with ROC-AUC, learning curves and SHAP.

  3. 03 Day 60

    Custom Object-Detection Pipeline

    Bounding-box-aware Albumentations, a YOLOv10 model trained via transfer learning, evaluated with mAP.

  4. 04 Day 75

    Transformer NMT from Scratch

    Multi-head attention from primitive matmuls, BPE, causal masks — trained on machine translation.

  5. 05 Day 90

    Autonomous Multi-Agent Research System

    Hybrid-search RAG, LangGraph multi-agent routing, a Python REPL tool, FastAPI + Streamlit, LangSmith and RAGAS.

  6. 06 Days 95–98

    Final Capstone & Graduation

    Scope a business problem, model it, deploy it behind FastAPI with a polished UI, then defend it in a 15-minute pitch.

  7. 07 Days 114–120

    Production ML API

    MLflow experiment tracking, serialised pipelines, a validated FastAPI service and a Dockerised deployment.

Full curriculum

Every session, day by day.

PDF brochure
Month 01 · Days 1–20

Python Foundations, OOP, & Data Engineering

Day 1Introduction to Programming & Environment Setup
  • Concepts: Differentiate between Algorithms (logic) and Programs (code).
  • Environment: Install Anaconda and configure VS Code/Jupyter.
  • Execution: Run your first interactive Python commands (print("Hello World")).
  • Virtual Environments: Introduce venv and conda to prevent package conflicts early on.
Day 2Variables, Data Types & I/O
  • Syntax: Master Python indentation, variable naming rules, and comments.
  • Core Types: Understand int, float, str, and bool natively.
  • Inspection: Use type() to check objects and id() to see memory addresses.
  • I/O: Capture dynamic user input via input() and explicitly type-cast variables.
Day 3String Manipulation & Formatting + Core Data Structures & Mutability
  • Indexing: Access characters and slice strings using [start:stop:step].
  • Methods: Apply .upper(), .lower(), .strip(), .replace(), and .split().
  • Formatting: Master modern f-strings for dynamic text injection.
  • Regex Intro: Use the re module for basic pattern matching and text normalization.
  • Lists & Tuples: Create ordered sequences. Compare mutable Lists vs. immutable Tuples.
  • Dicts & Sets: Implement key-value mappings and unique unordered sets.
  • Mutability: Understand why modifying a list changes it in memory, but modifying a string creates a new object.
  • Methods: Use .append(), .pop(), .keys(), and .items().
Day 4Operators & Control Flow
  • Operators: Apply Arithmetic (+, %, //), Comparison (==, >), and Logical (and, or, not).
  • Conditionals: Build complex branching logic using if, elif, and else.
  • Loops: Iterate over data using for loops and manage state with while loops.
  • Control: Master break, continue, and pass statements within loops.
Day 5Functions, Scope (LEGB) & Argument Unpacking
  • Definition: Create reusable logic blocks using def and return.
  • Arguments: Pass positional, keyword, and default parameters.
  • Flexibility: Build dynamic pipelines using *args and **kwargs.
  • Scope: Understand variable visibility via the LEGB rule.
Day 6Functional Programming & Comprehensions + File I/O & Exception Handling
  • Anonymous: Write single-line logic using lambda functions.
  • Mapping: Transform and filter arrays cleanly using map() and filter().
  • Comprehensions: Replace heavy loops with optimized List, Dict, and Set comprehensions.
  • Efficiency: Compare the execution speed of loops vs. comprehensions.
  • Files: Read and write raw TXT and CSV files natively.
  • Context: Use the with open() statement to ensure safe resource teardown.
  • Errors: Prevent code crashes using try, except, else, and finally blocks.
  • Custom Errors: raise custom Exceptions for strict data validation.
Day 7Object-Oriented Programming (OOP): Part 1
  • Blueprints: Define class structures and instantiate objects.
  • State: Initialize attributes using the __init__ constructor and self.
  • Inheritance: Pass behaviors from parent classes to child classes to avoid redundant code.
  • MRO: Understand Method Resolution Order in multiple inheritance.
Day 8Object-Oriented Programming (OOP): Part 2
  • Encapsulation: Protect internal variables using name mangling (__attr).
  • Magic Methods: Override dunders (__str__, __len__, __add__) to make custom classes behave like native types.
  • Properties: Use @property decorators for controlled variable access.
  • Polymorphism: Ensure identical method names behave differently across subclasses.
Day 9Decorators, Generators & Lazy Evaluation + CPython Internals & Memory Layout
  • Generators: Use yield to stream massive datasets without crashing RAM.
  • Decorators: Wrap functions with @ decorators to inject logic without altering core code.
  • Itertools: Build combinatoric pipelines using chain, cycle, and product.
  • Preservation: Use functools.wraps to keep function metadata intact.
  • Bytecode: Understand how Python compiles to .pyc and runs on the PVM.
  • References: Analyze memory pointers, reference counting, and garbage collection.
  • The GIL: Learn why the Global Interpreter Lock prevents true multi-threading in pure Python.
  • Profiling: Track memory leaks utilizing the tracemalloc library.
Day 10Concurrency: Threading, Multiprocessing & Asyncio
  • Threading: Handle network/I/O tasks via ThreadPoolExecutor.
  • Multiprocessing: Bypass the GIL for heavy math utilizing ProcessPoolExecutor.
  • Asyncio: Build single-threaded, non-blocking loops using async and await.
  • Safety: Prevent race conditions using Locks and Semaphores.
Day 11Advanced Packaging, Type Hints & Pydantic
  • Typing: Enforce strict parameter types using the typing module and mypy.
  • Validation: Ensure JSON data integrity natively using Pydantic schemas.
  • Boilerplate: Auto-generate class structures using @dataclass.
  • Modules: Structure large projects with __init__.py and pyproject.toml.
Day 12NumPy: Arrays, Broadcasting & Vectorization + Pandas Fundamentals & Data Structures
  • Tensors: Create N-dimensional matrices (np.zeros, np.arange).
  • Vectorization: Execute C-level mathematical operations natively without slow Python loops.
  • Broadcasting: Perform arithmetic mathematically on arrays of mismatched shapes.
  • Linear Algebra: Compute dot products (np.dot) and matrix multiplications.
  • Series/DataFrames: Master 1D and 2D tabular data structures.
  • Importing: Ingest pd.read_csv, pd.read_json, and pd.read_sql.
  • Inspection: Assess datasets rapidly utilizing .head(), .info(), and .describe().
  • Selection: Filter columns and rows explicitly via .loc[] and .iloc[].
Day 13Advanced Pandas: Cleaning & Aggregation
  • Missing Data: Impute or drop nulls using .fillna() and .dropna().
  • Transformations: Apply complex custom logic across rows via .apply().
  • GroupBy: Execute SQL-style aggregations utilizing .groupby() and .agg().
  • Dates: Parse and manipulate temporal features via the .dt accessor.
Day 14Data Merging & Automated Web Scraping
  • Combining: Join disparate datasets using pd.merge() (Inner, Left, Right).
  • Requests: Fetch raw HTML securely via the requests HTTP library.
  • Parsing: Extract targeted data tags using BeautifulSoup.
  • Dynamic: Automate browser interactions for JS-rendered sites via Selenium.
Day 15Code Testing & Logging + Capstone: End-to-End Extraction Pipeline
  • Unit Testing: Write robust test cases using the pytest framework.
  • Mocking: Simulate API responses to test functions in isolation.
  • Logging: Replace print() with the logging module (Info, Warning, Error, Critical).
  • Debugging: Master the pdb debugger to step through code execution dynamically.
  • Extraction: Write a scraper to collect raw data from a multi-page website.
  • Cleaning: Utilize Pandas to parse strings, handle missing values, and type-cast.
  • Architecture: Structure the code using strict OOP principles, Type Hints, and Decorators.
  • Output: Export the finalized, clean dataset to a SQLite database or Parquet file.
Day 16Data Visualization with Matplotlib
  • Core API: Build layouts via plt.subplots() rather than the state machine.
  • Plot Types: Generate line, bar, scatter, histogram, and pie charts.
  • Customization: Apply labels, legends, colormaps, and annotations.
  • Export: Save high-res publication figures using plt.savefig().
Day 17Data Visualization with Seaborn & Plotly
  • Seaborn: Plot distributions (boxplot, violinplot, heatmap, pairplot).
  • Plotly Express: Build interactive 3D scatters, animations, and maps.
  • Plotly Graph Objects: Gain fine-grained control over complex interactive plots.
  • Dash: Introduction to web-based interactive ML dashboard frameworks.
Day 18Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA) Framework + Descriptive Statistics: Central Tendency & Dispersion
  • Univariate: Analyze shape, skewness, and kurtosis via histograms and KDEs.
  • Bivariate: Identify feature-target correlations using point-biserial and scatter plots.
  • Multivariate: Detect multicollinearity using Variance Inflation Factor (VIF).
  • Automation: Rapidly generate reports using the ydata-profiling library.
  • Centrality: Calculate mean, median, mode, and geometric mean.
  • Spread: Measure variance, standard deviation, range, and Interquartile Range (IQR).
  • Outliers: Apply Tukey's fences (Q1 − 1.5 × IQR, Q3 + 1.5 × IQR).
  • Dependencies: Compute covariance and Pearson correlation mathematically.
Day 19Probability Foundations & Bayes' Theorem
  • Axioms: Define sample spaces, unions, intersections, and conditional probability.
  • Bayes' Theorem: Compute Posterior from Prior, Likelihood, and Evidence.
  • Distributions: Differentiate Discrete vs. Continuous random variables.
  • ML Application: Connect Bayes' to Naive Bayes classifiers and updating.
Day 20Discrete & Continuous Probability Distributions
  • Discrete: Model outcomes using Bernoulli, Binomial, and Poisson distributions.
  • The Gaussian Curve: Master the Normal distribution and Z-score standardization.
  • Heavy Tails: Apply the Student's t-distribution for small-sample continuous data.
  • Computation: Generate PDFs/PMFs programmatically using scipy.stats.
Month 02 · Days 21–40

Statistics, EDA & Foundational ML Models

Day 21Central Limit Theorem & Sampling + Correlation Analysis & Feature Relationships
  • CLT: Prove that sample means converge to a Normal distribution regardless of shape.
  • Standard Error: Calculate precision using SE = σ/√n.
  • Bootstrapping: Generate non-parametric sampling distributions via resampling.
  • Strategies: Execute Random, Stratified, and Cluster sampling methodologies.
  • Parametric vs Non-Parametric: Compare Pearson's r against Spearman's rank ρ.
  • Categorical Links: Compute point-biserial and Phi coefficients.
  • Information Theory: Calculate Mutual Information for non-linear feature selection.
  • Causality: Identify spurious correlations and understand Simpson's Paradox.
Day 22Hypothesis Testing: Framework & p-values
  • Framework: Define the Null (H₀) and Alternative (H₁) hypotheses clearly.
  • Risk Matrix: Quantify Type I (False Positive) and Type II (False Negative) errors.
  • Metrics: Calculate p-values, significance levels (α), and statistical power (1-β).
  • Confidence Bounds: Construct 95% CIs using Z-values and t-values.
Day 23Statistical Testing: Parametric & Non-Parametric
  • Mean Comparisons: Execute Z-tests, independent T-tests, and paired T-tests.
  • Multi-Group: Run One-Way and Two-Way ANOVA utilizing the F-statistic.
  • Rank Tests: Use Mann-Whitney U and Kruskal-Wallis for non-normal data.
  • Categorical: Execute Chi-Square tests of independence and A/B test setups.
Day 24Intro to ML Taxonomy & The Bias-Variance Tradeoff + Feature Engineering & Scaling
  • Taxonomy: Define Supervised, Unsupervised, Semi-Supervised, and RL paradigms.
  • Workflow: Map the pipeline from EDA to Deployment and Monitoring.
  • Tradeoff: Mathematically decompose MSE into Bias², Variance, and Noise.
  • Mitigation: Counter underfitting/overfitting via regularization and ensembles.
  • Scaling: Normalize features via StandardScaler, MinMaxScaler, and RobustScaler.
  • Encoding: Apply One-Hot and Target encoding using get_dummies and scikit-learn.
  • Imbalance: Generate synthetic minority instances using SMOTE and ADASYN.
  • Pipelines: Automate workflows safely using ColumnTransformer and Pipeline.
Day 25Model Validation & Leakage Prevention
  • Splitting: Implement strict Train/Validation/Test splits with class stratification.
  • CV Methods: Execute k-Fold, LOOCV, and TimeSeriesSplit.
  • Data Leakage: Identify and prevent temporal violations and pre-split scaling.
  • Nested CV: Tune hyperparameters without optimistic bias via nested loops.
Day 26Linear Regression: OLS & Diagnostics
  • OLS Math: Solve regression weights using closed-form algebra.
  • Assumptions: Validate the Gauss-Markov theorems (linearity, homoscedasticity).
  • Diagnostics: Plot residuals vs. fitted values and calculate Cook's Distance.
  • Evaluation: Calculate MSE, RMSE, MAE, and Adjusted R2 mathematically.
Day 27Multiple Regression, Collinearity & Regularization + Logistic Regression & Decision Boundaries
  • Multivariate: Interpret partial derivative coefficients in multiple dimensions.
  • Collinearity: Detect feature correlation using VIF and mitigate via PCA.
  • Optimization: Implement Batch, Stochastic (SGD), and Mini-Batch Gradient Descent.
  • Regularization: Induce sparsity via L1 (Lasso) and shrink weights via L2 (Ridge).
  • Sigmoid: Squash linear outputs into probabilities using σ(z) = 1/(1 + e−z).
  • Interpretability: Extract log-odds and convert to multiplicative Odds Ratios.
  • Optimization: Minimize Binary Cross-Entropy loss via Maximum Likelihood.
  • Implementation: Train via LogisticRegression using lbfgs and saga solvers.
Day 28Classification Evaluation Metrics
  • Confusion Matrix: Map True/False Positives and Negatives.
  • Ratios: Calculate Precision (purity), Recall (completeness), and the F1-Score.
  • ROC-AUC: Evaluate threshold-independent performance using TPR vs. FPR.
  • Imbalance Tools: Plot Precision-Recall curves and calculate Matthews Correlation.
Day 29Naive Bayes Classifiers & Text Applications
  • Bayesian Math: Apply conditional independence assumptions for rapid O(n · p) fitting.
  • Variants: Use GaussianNB for continuous data and MultinomialNB for NLP counts.
  • Smoothing: Implement Laplace additive smoothing to handle zero-probability features.
  • NLP Pipelines: Combine Naive Bayes with TF-IDF vectorization for text sorting.
Day 30K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN) + Support Vector Machines (SVM)
  • Lazy Learning: Classify via majority vote without an explicit training phase.
  • Metrics: Calculate Euclidean, Manhattan (L1), and Cosine similarities.
  • Hyperparameters: Tune k using cross-validation to balance bias/variance.
  • Scaling: Accelerate search queries using KD-trees and Ball trees.
  • Hyperplanes: Maximize the geometric margin between separable classes.
  • Soft Margins: Introduce slack variables (ξ) to handle non-linearly separable data.
  • Kernel Trick: Map features to infinite dimensions via Linear, Polynomial, and RBF kernels.
  • Hyperparameter C: Tune the strictness of the margin constraint (bias vs variance).
Day 31Decision Trees: CART, Information Gain & Splitting
  • Splitting Logic: Partition features by minimizing Gini Impurity or Entropy.
  • CART Algorithm: Perform exhaustive greedy search for optimal threshold splits.
  • Importance: Extract normalized feature importance scores based on impurity drops.
  • Visualization: Plot hierarchical splits utilizing sklearn.tree.plot_tree.
Day 32Tree Pruning & Hyperparameter Tuning
  • Overfitting: Understand how unconstrained trees memorize noise.
  • Pruning: Constrain growth using max_depth, min_samples_leaf, and ccp_alpha.
  • Tuning Pipeline: Automate optimal parameter discovery using GridSearchCV.
  • Decision Boundaries: Visualize orthogonal, step-wise decision boundaries mathematically.
Day 33Ensemble Methods Part 1: Bagging & Random Forests + Ensemble Methods Part 2: Boosting Foundations
  • Ensemble Theory: Combine weak learners to build a highly robust generalized model.
  • Bagging: Train independent models on bootstrapped data subsets.
  • Random Forests: Force spatial decorrelation via random feature subset selection.
  • OOB Scoring: Validate model performance dynamically using Out-of-Bag data metrics.
  • Boosting Theory: Train sequential models to explicitly correct predecessor residuals.
  • AdaBoost: Dynamically reweight misclassified instances to force mathematical attention.
  • Gradient Boosting: Fit trees directly to the negative gradients of any differentiable loss function.
  • Learning Rate: Balance the shrinkage parameter against the number of estimators.
Day 34Advanced Boosting: XGBoost, LightGBM & CatBoost
  • XGBoost: Leverage second-order Taylor expansions and strict L1/L2 leaf regularization.
  • LightGBM: Achieve extreme speed via histogram-based binning and leaf-wise node growth.
  • CatBoost: Handle high-cardinality categorical targets natively using ordered boosting algorithms.
  • Implementation: Train APIs utilizing xgb.XGBClassifier() and lgb.LGBMClassifier().
Day 35K-Means Clustering & Centroid Initialization
  • Lloyd's Algorithm: Alternate iteratively between centroid assignment and WCSS minimization.
  • Initialization: Prevent local-minima traps using probabilistic k-means++.

  • Interface: Build an async streaming Streamlit interface supported by a secure FastAPI backend.
  • Monitoring: Complete with deep LangSmith observability and automated RAGAS evaluations.
Day 91Multimodal Models & Vision-Language
  • CLIP: Understand Contrastive Language-Image Pretraining architecture.
  • Embeddings: Align text and image vectors into a shared mathematical space.
  • Generation: Deploy visual-question answering pipelines using specialized LLMs.
Day 92AI Ethics, Bias Mitigation & Fairness
  • Disparate Impact: Identify and measure hidden bias in historical training datasets.
  • Fairness Metrics: Calculate Equal Opportunity and Demographic Parity natively.
  • Red Teaming: Actively probe generative models for unsafe or restricted outputs.
Day 93Model Security & Adversarial Robustness + Federated Learning Foundations
  • Attacks: Understand Fast Gradient Sign Method (FGSM) and prompt injection.
  • Defense: Train models with adversarial examples to increase robustness boundaries.
  • Sanitization: Scrub inbound user prompts securely before reaching the inference engine.
  • Decentralization: Train models collaboratively without centralizing raw user data.
  • Aggregation: Apply Federated Averaging mathematically to update global weights.
  • Use Cases: Analyze implementations in healthcare and cross-device personalization.
Day 94ML System Design Frameworks
  • Framework: Master the 5-step approach (Requirements, Metrics, Architecture, Data, Scale).
  • Trade-offs: Justify architectural decisions (Batch vs Streaming, CPU vs GPU).
  • Communication: Lead whiteboarding discussions regarding single points of failure.
Day 95Capstone Phase 1: Problem Scoping
  • Ideation: Define a high-impact business problem solvable via Advanced ML.
  • Requirements: Draft strict technical specifications and success metrics.
  • Sourcing: Identify, acquire, and validate necessary raw datasets.
Day 96Capstone Phase 2: Data & Modeling + Capstone Phase 3: Deployment Architecture
  • Pipelines: Construct automated EDA and feature engineering loops.
  • Training: Train, tune, and log champion models utilizing robust cross-validation.
  • Validation: Defend model selection based on mathematical metrics.
  • API: Wrap the final serialized model natively in a strictly typed FastAPI container.
  • Local Run: Ensure seamless local execution and API endpoint pinging.
  • Documentation: Finalize README.md, architecture diagrams, and comprehensive API docs.
Day 97Capstone Phase 4: UI/UX & Polish
  • Frontend: Build a highly interactive frontend utilizing Streamlit or Gradio.
  • User Experience: Ensure latency remains low and error messages are clear.
  • Portfolio: Curate a professional, production-ready GitHub repository.
Day 98Capstone Presentation & Industry Graduation
  • Pitch: Deliver a 15-minute technical presentation to stakeholders.
  • Q&A: Defend architectural, systemic, and mathematical choices under intense scrutiny.
  • CORE GRADUATION: Officially conclude the core AIML engineering program!
Day 99Big-O & Problem Solving Mindset + Arrays & Memory Basics
  • Complexity: Analyze basic Time & Space Complexity (O(1), O(n), O(log n), O(n2)).
  • Relevance: Understand why efficiency matters for large ML datasets.
  • Mindset: Develop pattern recognition skills to map coding problems logically.
  • Data Structures: Understand Python lists as dynamic arrays in memory.
  • Techniques: Implement foundational Two-Pointer techniques for traversal.
  • Problems: Solve basic array problems like Two Sum and reversing an array.
Day 100String Manipulation Logic
  • Immutability: Understand how string manipulation affects memory.
  • Techniques: Apply the Sliding Window technique to find substrings.
  • Problems: Find longest non-repeating substrings and valid palindromes.
Month 06 · Days 101–120

Capstone Conclusion, DSA, SQL & MLOps

Day 101Basic Searching Algorithms
  • Linear Search: Understand standard O(N) iterative searching.
  • Binary Search: Implement O(log N) search on sorted data.
  • Intuition: Relate binary search concepts to hyperparameter space halving.
Day 102Basic Sorting Algorithms + Linked Lists Foundations
  • Algorithms: Understand Bubble Sort, Selection Sort, and basic Merge Sort.
  • Time/Space: Compare the O(N2) worst cases versus O(N log N) optimization.
  • Python API: Utilize Python's internal sort() and sorted() efficiently.
  • Structures: Understand Singly Linked List nodes and pointers.
  • Techniques: Traverse, insert, and delete nodes without native array indexing.
  • Problems: Reverse a linked list manually and detect basic cycles.
Day 103Stacks & Queues
  • Structures: Understand LIFO (Stacks) and FIFO (Queues) principles.
  • Implementation: Build stacks using lists and queues using collections.deque.
  • Applications: Solve valid parentheses and basic sequential tracking problems.
Day 104Hashmaps & Sets
  • Dictionaries: Deep dive into internal hashing mechanics and O(1) lookups.
  • Sets: Perform fast containment checks and deduplication explicitly.
  • Problems: Utilize frequency counting (collections.Counter) for rapid math.
Day 105Introduction to Recursion + Basics of Binary Trees
  • Mechanics: Understand base cases and map basic execution flows.
  • Memory: Visualize Call Stack execution during deep recursive functions.
  • Problems: Calculate factorials and the Fibonacci sequence recursively.
  • Structures: Build basic binary tree nodes and link children.
  • Traversals: Implement Inorder, Preorder, and Postorder traversals natively.
  • Search: Understand the basic properties of a Binary Search Tree (BST).
Day 106SQL Fundamentals and DDL
  • RDBMS & SELECT: Understand the relational model. Master SELECT and WHERE filtering.
  • DDL: Structure databases: CREATE TABLE, ALTER TABLE, and DROP TABLE.
  • Constraints: Enforce integrity with Primary/Foreign Keys, UNIQUE, and NOT NULL.
Day 107Data Manipulation & Retrieval
  • DML: Insert (INSERT INTO), update (UPDATE), and delete (DELETE) data.
  • Transactions: Maintain consistency using COMMIT and ROLLBACK.
  • DQL: Use ORDER BY for sorting and DISTINCT to extract unique values.
Day 108Aggregation & Grouping + Advanced Filtering & Set Operations
  • Math: Utilize COUNT, SUM, and AVG for column-level calculations.
  • Extremes: Use MIN and MAX to find extremes within datasets.
  • Grouping: Aggregate distinct categories via GROUP BY and filter them using HAVING.
  • Filtering: Apply logical operators (AND, OR) and special operators (LIKE, IN, BETWEEN).
  • Set Operators: Combine multiple queries using UNION, UNION ALL, INTERSECT, and EXCEPT.
  • Execution Order: Understand how SQL conceptually executes written commands.
Day 109Relational Data Joins
  • Inner/Outer Joins: Master INNER JOIN, LEFT, RIGHT, and FULL OUTER JOIN handling unmatched rows.
  • Advanced Joins: Explore non-equi joins, CROSS JOIN (Cartesian), and SELF-JOIN.
  • Architecture: Understand why normalized relational schemas require heavy joining.
Day 110Built-in Functions & Null Handling
  • Strings: Manipulate text (SUBSTRING, LENGTH, UPPER, TRIM).
  • Nulls: Address missing data securely using IS NULL and COALESCE/ISNULL.
  • Dates: Extract parts, calculate differences (DATEDIFF), and perform date arithmetic.
Day 111Conditional Logic & Subqueries + CTEs & Procedures
  • Aliases: Use column and table ALIASES to write cleaner SQL code.
  • Logic: Implement conditional mapping natively using the CASE expression.
  • Subqueries: Write independent subqueries and use EXISTS for correlated subqueries.
  • Procedures: Encapsulate basic SQL logic strictly inside Stored Procedures.
  • CTEs: Define named, temporary result sets (WITH clause) to simplify complex reads.
  • Recursion: Understand the concept of Recursive CTEs conceptually vs standard queries.
Day 112Window Functions (Part 1)
  • Concept: Introduce calculations across a defined set of table rows dynamically.
  • Ranking: Master strict ranking functions: RANK, DENSE_RANK, and ROW_NUMBER.
  • Application: Rank distinct rows without grouping them down into single aggregated lines.
Day 113Window Functions (Part 2)
  • Partitions: Use PARTITION BY to establish exact analytical window boundaries.
  • Analytics: Calculate running totals and lagged/leaded values using LAG/LEAD.
  • Time-Series: Utilize moving averages natively within SQL for financial/data analysis.
Day 114Introduction to MLOps + Data & Code Versioning
  • Lifecycle: Map the transition from local Jupyter Notebooks to strict production pipelines.
  • Concepts: Understand Continuous Integration, Continuous Delivery, and Continuous Training (CI/CD/CT).
  • Necessity: Discuss why models degrade over time and require operational supervision.
  • Code: Overview foundational Git commands (commit, push, branch) for ML scripts.
  • Data Control: Understand the strict necessity of Data Version Control (DVC) conceptually.
  • Reproducibility: Ensure environments and datasets can be mirrored by any other engineer.
Day 115Experiment Tracking Basics
  • Tracking: Track hyperparameter choices, metric outputs, and random seeds programmatically.
  • Comparison: Understand how comparing isolated experiments prevents "lost" champion models.
  • Metadata: Log strict metadata associated with every specific training run.
Day 116Introduction to MLflow
  • Server: Launch and navigate a local MLflow tracking server dashboard.
  • Logging: Utilize mlflow.log_param and mlflow.log_metric inside Python training loops.
  • Autolog: Implement mlflow.autolog() for rapid, out-of-the-box framework tracking.
Day 117Model Serialization & Packaging + Introduction to REST APIs
  • Serialization: Save and load trained ML models natively utilizing pickle and joblib.
  • Pipelines: Bundle preprocessors (scalers/encoders) securely with the model object via sklearn.pipeline.
  • Dependencies: Extract a precise requirements.txt file to prevent critical version drift.
  • Concepts: Understand client-server architecture, HTTP verbs (GET/POST), and status codes.
  • JSON: Map Python dictionaries natively into structured JSON payload transfers.
  • Inference: Translate local model.predict() logic into a networked request-response cycle.
Day 118Building Basic APIs with FastAPI
  • Framework: Initialize an asynchronous FastAPI application locally.
  • Endpoints: Create a strict @app.post("/predict") route to ingest feature data.
  • Pydantic: Enforce inbound JSON data structures mathematically using Pydantic validation schemas.
Day 119Testing & Validating the API
  • Swagger UI: Test the endpoint interactively via the automatically generated Swagger docs (/docs).
  • Postman/cURL: Ping the local ML server securely using external networking tools.
  • Error Handling: Return proper 400 Bad Request codes for malformed data inputs.
Day 120Introduction to Docker + Writing a Dockerfile for ML
  • Containerization: Understand isolation constraints versus traditional heavy virtual machines.
  • Images/Containers: Differentiate between a static Docker Image and a running Container.
  • Commands: Use basic CLI tools like docker build, docker run, and docker ps.
  • Declarations: Write a basic Dockerfile explicitly tailored for ML (FROM python:3.10, COPY, CMD).
  • Execution: Build the image and run the isolated API container locally, mapping internal ports.
  • Cloud Intro: Discuss conceptual pathways for pushing this container to AWS/GCP for public access.

FAQ

About Applied AI & ML.

Have a question that isn’t covered here? Ask an advisor directly.

Ask on WhatsApp
Is this program suitable for beginners?

It starts with Python foundations, but the pace and depth are engineering-grade — concurrency, CPython internals, Transformers from scratch and MLOps. Comfort with logical thinking and maths will help you get the most from it.

Which deep-learning framework is used?

TensorFlow and Keras — tensors, GradientTape, custom training loops, tf.data pipelines, CNNs, ResNets, transfer learning, YOLO, segmentation and Vision Transformers.

How deep does the GenAI coverage go?

Attention, QKV and positional encoding, building a Transformer from scratch, GPT-style decoding, advanced prompting and ReAct, vector databases, advanced RAG, MCP tool calling, LoRA/QLoRA fine-tuning and RLHF/DPO alignment.

Does it prepare me for interviews?

Yes. Month 6 covers data structures and algorithms — Big-O, searching, sorting, linked lists, stacks, queues, hashmaps, recursion and trees — plus SQL and ML system design frameworks.

Will I learn to deploy models?

Yes — Git and DVC, MLflow tracking, serialisation, REST APIs with FastAPI and Pydantic, testing with Swagger and Postman, and Docker containers.
